title: Screening rules

scenes.say: Screening rules decide how Sentinel checks your customers: which AML hits count, how often customers are screened again, and what happens to a forged document. Let's walk through them.
Click Settings, then the Screening rules tab. A new organization starts with Sentinel's standard rules, so nothing changes until you save here.

Under AML matching, the match threshold sets how close a name must be to count as a hit. The default is seventy percent. Raising it cuts false positives, but can miss spelling variants of Kenyan and Somali names.
Then tick your high-risk PEP classes, Class 1 and Class 2 by default. A case with a PEP hit in a ticked class opens as high priority, so it gets your shortest deadline.

show.highlight: field:Class 1: national / head of state level

scenes.say: False-positive memory is on by default. When a reviewer approves an AML case, its hits are remembered as cleared for that customer, and aren't raised again unless they get more severe. To bring a hit back, an Admin or Reviewer clicks Forget in the list.
With AI hit review on, Sentinel's AI compares the customer with each hit as soon as a case opens, and recommends what to do. It only recommends. Your reviewers decide.

show.zoom: field:Review hits with AI when a case opens

scenes.say: Face match compares the selfie with the ID photo, and never rejects on its own. Searching for the same face among your customers is off by default. It keeps face templates, which are biometric data, so check your privacy notice first.

The fraud network compares ID numbers, phone numbers and emails across your checks. Turn on Join the Sentinel network to compare them with other organizations too. Only keyed fingerprints are compared, never the numbers themselves.
Next, set how often customers are reviewed by risk rating: every 12, 24 or 36 months by default. Below that are your transaction monitoring thresholds, in US dollars.

show.scroll: card:Customer risk rating and periodic review

scenes.say: Choose how often monitored customers are re-screened: daily, weekly or monthly. Then, under Documents, choose whether an AI-generated document is rejected automatically, or sent to your team for review.
When you're happy, click Save changes. New rules apply from that moment, and past results keep their verdict. Each save is recorded in the audit log.
Those are your screening rules. To learn more, open chapter A7 in Help, Screening rules.
